question: A community nurse testing the well water of a village finds a heavy growth of coliform bacteria at 120 counts per 100 mL. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take?
option_1: Note the result and plan a fresh visit next year
option_2: Ask the families to store the water in open pots
option_3: Report the finding and tell the families to boil their drinking water
option_4: Tell the children that the water is safe to drink
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report the finding and tell the families to boil their drinking water

Clinical Rationale: Coliform bacteria in the water point to sewage contamination, so the result is reported and the families are told to boil the water before drinking.

Key Clue: coliform bacteria in the village well water

Priority Principle: Safe drinking water

Why Not Others: (a) A visit next year leaves the danger for long; (b) Open storage lets the water be spoiled again; (d) The water is poisoned and not safe to drink.

PGI Exam Trap: The children are told that the well water is safe to drink.

5-Second Recall: Report the growth and tell the families to boil the water.

PNC Exam Pearl: Coliform in the well means boil the water.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which food is the MOST appropriate to give him for a low iron level.
option_1: White rice with plain water and salt
option_2: Green leafy vegetables with a piece of jaggery
option_3: A sweet milk pudding served cold
option_4: Tea with a lot of sugar and milk
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Green leafy vegetables with a piece of jaggery

Clinical Rationale: Green leafy vegetables with jaggery carry plenty of iron, which helps the body to build new blood.

Key Clue: foods rich in iron

Priority Principle: Iron rich food

Why Not Others: (a) White rice with water has very little iron; (c) A milk pudding is poor in iron; (d) Tea with sugar adds little iron.

PGI Exam Trap: A milk pudding is chosen as the BEST source of iron.

5-Second Recall: Green leafy vegetables with jaggery are rich in iron.

PNC Exam Pearl: Greens and jaggery build the blood.

question: A nurse caring for an elderly woman on the ward who lies still for many hours is asked which statement about pressure sore prevention is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The bony points where the skin rests are checked and shifted often
option_2: The skin is kept wet with a warm cloth all day
option_3: She is left in one position so that she can rest
option_4: The bed sheet is kept loose and crumpled below her
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The bony points where the skin rests are checked and shifted often

Clinical Rationale: Pressure sores start where bone presses the skin, so the bony points are checked and her position is shifted to keep the skin safe.

Key Clue: an elderly woman lying still for many hours

Priority Principle: Pressure sore prevention

Why Not Others: (b) Wet skin breaks down more easily; (c) One position presses the same skin for long; (d) Crumpled sheets rub and damage the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: She is left in one position so that she can rest.

5-Second Recall: The bony points are checked and she is shifted often.

PNC Exam Pearl: Still and bony, skin breaks.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has heart failure notes that his ankles are swollen and he gains 2 kg in a week. Which finding is the MOST important for the nurse to report?
option_1: A calm mood through the whole day
option_2: A steady pulse of 78 bpm with warm hands
option_3: A good appetite at all the meal times
option_4: Increasing breathlessness with a rising weight
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Increasing breathlessness with a rising weight

Clinical Rationale: Swollen ankles with a fast weight gain point to fluid building up, so increasing breathlessness is reported at once as the heart fails further.

Key Clue: a weight gain of 2 kg in a week with heart failure

Priority Principle: Fluid overload

Why Not Others: (a) A calm mood is not a warning sign; (b) A steady pulse of 78 bpm is normal; (c) A good appetite does not show fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: The steady pulse is reported as the danger sign.

5-Second Recall: Increasing breathlessness with a rising weight is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fast weight gain means fluid in the body.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is one day after a heart attack notes a new harsh murmur and sudden breathlessness. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note the murmur for the ward round
option_2: Give him a hot drink and let him rest
option_3: Ask him to walk to the bathroom
option_4: Call for help and stay with him
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Call for help and stay with him

Clinical Rationale: A new murmur with sudden breathlessness after a heart attack points to a torn heart valve, so help is called and he is NOT left alone.

Key Clue: a new murmur with sudden breathlessness after a heart attack

Priority Principle: Ruptured heart valve

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for the round misses the danger; (b) A hot drink does not treat the danger; (c) Walking strains the damaged heart.

PGI Exam Trap: The murmur is noted and the ward round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Call for help and stay with him.

PNC Exam Pearl: New murmur after a heart attack means call for help.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the postnatal ward is asked which statement about breastfeeding is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The baby is put to the breast within the FIRST hour
option_2: The FIRST thick yellow milk is thrown away
option_3: The baby is fed only when it cries loudly
option_4: The mother is asked to rest and skip night feeds
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The baby is put to the breast within the FIRST hour

Clinical Rationale: Putting the baby to the breast within the FIRST hour gives it the FIRST thick milk, which carries protection against illness.

Key Clue: the start of breastfeeding

Priority Principle: Early breastfeeding

Why Not Others: (b) The first yellow milk is rich and is not thrown; (c) Feeding on demand is better than on loud cries; (d) Night feeds are needed for the milk supply.

PGI Exam Trap: The FIRST thick yellow milk is thrown away.

5-Second Recall: The baby is put to the breast within the first hour.

PNC Exam Pearl: First hour, first milk.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a normal urine output is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is about ten litres in a day
option_2: It is about one and a half litres in a day
option_3: It is the same colour as dark tea
option_4: It stops completely after an operation
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It is about one and a half litres in a day

Clinical Rationale: A normal adult passes about one and a half litres of urine in a day, which shows the kidneys are working well.

Key Clue: the normal daily urine output

Priority Principle: Urine output

Why Not Others: (a) Ten litres a day is far too much; (c) Dark tea colour suggests concentrated urine; (d) No urine after an operation must be reported.

PGI Exam Trap: Ten litres a day is called a normal output.

5-Second Recall: About one and a half litres in a day is normal.

PNC Exam Pearl: One and a half litres, clear and pale.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the labour room notes that after the baby is born the womb is soft and the pad is soaked with blood within 5 minutes. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Set the pad aside and watch the bleeding
option_2: Give her a warm drink and wait
option_3: Rub the womb and call the doctor at once
option_4: Help her to walk to the bathroom
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Rub the womb and call the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A soft womb with a soaked pad after delivery points to heavy bleeding, so the womb is rubbed up and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: a soft womb with a soaked pad after delivery

Priority Principle: Postpartum haemorrhage

Why Not Others: (a) Watching the pad lets her lose more blood; (b) A warm drink does not stop the bleeding; (d) Walking may make the bleeding worse.

PGI Exam Trap: The pad is set aside and the bleeding is watched.

5-Second Recall: Rub the womb and call the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Soft womb and soaked pad mean brisk bleeding.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a chest injury notes that one side of his chest does NOT move with the other during breathing. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask him to take a deep breath and walk
option_2: Check his breathing and give oxygen
option_3: Bind the chest tightly with a cloth
option_4: Leave him and note it for the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check his breathing and give oxygen

Clinical Rationale: A chest that does NOT move on one side after an injury points to air in the chest cavity, so his breathing is checked and oxygen given at once.

Key Clue: one side of the chest NOT moving after an injury

Priority Principle: Air in the chest

Why Not Others: (a) Walking uses more oxygen and strains him; (c) Tight binding stops the chest from moving; (d) Waiting lets the low oxygen worsen.

PGI Exam Trap: The chest is bound tightly with a cloth.

5-Second Recall: Check his breathing and give oxygen.

PNC Exam Pearl: One side still means air in the chest.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is shown a consent form for an operation that she herself has dated and signed while drowsy. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Report it so that fresh consent is taken when she is alert
option_2: Keep the form as it stands and go ahead
option_3: Ask the family to sign in her place at once
option_4: Note the form and plan the operation for today
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Report it so that fresh consent is taken when she is alert

Clinical Rationale: Consent signed while the woman was drowsy is of no value, so it is reported and fresh consent is taken when she is fully alert.

Key Clue: a consent form signed while drowsy

Priority Principle: Valid consent

Why Not Others: (b) A drowsy signature does not stand as consent; (c) The family cannot sign for a competent adult; (d) The operation should wait for proper consent.

PGI Exam Trap: The drowsy signature is kept and the operation goes ahead.

5-Second Recall: Report it so that fresh consent is taken when she is alert.

PNC Exam Pearl: Drowsy signature, no consent.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a sterile field is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The field is kept near a busy doorway
option_2: The field stays sterile after it is left open
option_3: A dry field is touched with wet gloves
option_4: Anything below the level of the waist is treated as spoiled
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Anything below the level of the waist is treated as spoiled

Clinical Rationale: In a sterile field anything below the level of the waist is out of sight and is treated as spoiled, so it is NOT used.

Key Clue: the rules for a sterile field

Priority Principle: Sterile field

Why Not Others: (a) A busy doorway carries dust onto it; (b) An open field picks up germs from the air; (c) Wet gloves soak the field and spoil it.

PGI Exam Trap: The field is left open and is still called sterile.

5-Second Recall: Anything below the waist is treated as spoiled.

PNC Exam Pearl: Below the waist means out of play.

question: A nurse manager on the ward must hand a task to the nursing assistant at the start of the shift. Which task is the MOST appropriate to delegate?
option_1: Deciding the drug dose for a child
option_2: Giving an injection to a sick woman
option_3: Recording the weight of a stable man
option_4: Taking the key for a controlled drug
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Recording the weight of a stable man

Clinical Rationale: Recording the weight of a stable client is a simple task that can be handed to the assistant, while drug work stays with the nurse.

Key Clue: which task to hand to the nursing assistant

Priority Principle: Task delegation

Why Not Others: (a) A drug dose is never decided by an assistant; (b) An injection needs a trained nurse; (d) Controlled drugs are kept with the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: The injection is handed to the nursing assistant.

5-Second Recall: Recording the weight of a stable client is delegated.

PNC Exam Pearl: Simple and safe, give it away.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who has a high fever notes a stiff neck and a rash that does NOT fade when pressed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Sponge the child with cold water and wait
option_2: Give a mild pain killer and let the child sleep
option_3: Call the doctor at once and start the care
option_4: Note the rash for the morning round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Call the doctor at once and start the care

Clinical Rationale: A stiff neck with a rash that does NOT fade in a febrile child points to a serious brain infection, so the doctor is called at once.

Key Clue: a stiff neck with a rash that does NOT fade

Priority Principle: Meningitis

Why Not Others: (a) Cold sponging does not treat the infection; (b) Sleep lets the infection spread unchecked; (d) Waiting for the round delays the treatment.

PGI Exam Trap: The rash is noted and the morning round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Call the doctor at once and start the care.

PNC Exam Pearl: Stiff neck and fixed rash mean call now.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about hand hygiene is NOT correct.
option_1: The hands are washed after touching any body fluid
option_2: The hands are washed before and after touching a client
option_3: Jewellery is removed so that the hands are cleaned fully
option_4: An alcohol rub is used when the hands are visibly soiled
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) An alcohol rub is used when the hands are visibly soiled

Clinical Rationale: An alcohol rub does NOT clean hands that are visibly soiled, so washing with soap and water is used for dirty hands.

Key Clue: the correct use of hand hygiene

Priority Principle: Hand hygiene

Why Not Others: (a) Washing after body fluid contact is correct; (b) Washing before and after care is correct; (c) Removing jewellery helps proper cleaning.

PGI Exam Trap: An alcohol rub is called enough for visibly soiled hands.

5-Second Recall: Washing with soap and water is needed for soiled hands.

PNC Exam Pearl: Soiled hands need soap, not a rub.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who has a leg ulcer is asked which statement about an ulcer from poor arteries is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The pain is worse when the leg is raised in bed
option_2: A firm bandage is put on the leg to heal it
option_3: The pain eases when she walks about the ward
option_4: The leg is kept up high so that it heals
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The pain is worse when the leg is raised in bed

Clinical Rationale: An ulcer from poor arteries hurts more when the leg is raised, because the flow of blood to the foot falls still further.

Key Clue: the signs of a leg ulcer from poor arteries

Priority Principle: Arterial leg ulcer

Why Not Others: (b) A firm bandage is used for vein ulcers; (c) Walking often makes the pain worse; (d) Keeping the leg high worsens the flow.

PGI Exam Trap: A firm bandage is put on the leg to heal an arterial ulcer.

5-Second Recall: The pain is worse when the leg is raised in bed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Raise the leg, worse the pain.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is started on an oxygen mask notes that his lips become pink and his breathing eases. Which finding is the MOST likely for the nurse to expect?
option_1: A falling oxygen level in the blood
option_2: A rising oxygen level in the blood
option_3: A rising level of acid in the blood
option_4: A falling level of sugar in the blood
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A rising oxygen level in the blood

Clinical Rationale: With oxygen the lips turn pink and the breathing eases, which shows the level of oxygen in the blood is rising.

Key Clue: pink lips with easier breathing on oxygen

Priority Principle: Rising oxygen

Why Not Others: (a) The oxygen level is rising, not falling; (c) Acid in the blood is not shown by pink lips; (d) Blood sugar is not the level that rises here.

PGI Exam Trap: A falling oxygen level is expected with pink lips.

5-Second Recall: A rising oxygen level in the blood is expected.

PNC Exam Pearl: Pink lips mean more oxygen.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is shown a monitor strip with a flat line and no beats while he is awake and talking. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Check him and his leads at once
option_2: Give him a strong pain killer and wait
option_3: Ask him to walk to test the monitor
option_4: Note the strip and change the monitor
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check him and his leads at once

Clinical Rationale: A flat monitor line in a man who is awake and talking points to a loose lead and NOT to a stopped heart, so he and his leads are checked at once.

Key Clue: a flat monitor line in an awake man

Priority Principle: Loose monitor lead

Why Not Others: (b) A pain killer does not answer a flat line; (c) Walking does not test the monitor lead; (d) Changing the monitor misses the true cause.

PGI Exam Trap: The flat strip is taken as a stopped heart at once.

5-Second Recall: Check him and his leads at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Awake and talking means check the leads.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to remove a soiled dressing from a wound. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Remove the dressing FIRST and then clean the hands
option_2: Clean the hands, wear gloves, then remove the dressing
option_3: Wear gloves, remove the dressing, then clean the hands
option_4: Remove the dressing with bare hands to save gloves
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean the hands, wear gloves, then remove the dressing

Clinical Rationale: The nurse cleans the hands, wears gloves, and then removes the dressing, so that the wound is cared for without spreading germs.

Key Clue: the steps for removing a soiled dressing

Priority Principle: Wound dressing order

Why Not Others: (a) The hands are cleaned before the dressing is touched; (c) Hand cleaning comes first of all; (d) Bare hands carry germs into the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: The dressing is removed with bare hands to save gloves.

5-Second Recall: Clean the hands, wear gloves, then remove the dressing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean, glove, then remove.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a chest drain notes that the tube has come out of his chest. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Leave the opening and note it for the round
option_2: Push the tube back into the chest at once
option_3: Cover the opening with a sterile dressing and call for help
option_4: Ask him to walk to test his breathing
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Cover the opening with a sterile dressing and call for help

Clinical Rationale: When a chest drain falls out, the opening is covered at once with a sterile dressing so that air does NOT enter and trap in the chest.

Key Clue: a chest drain tube that has fallen out

Priority Principle: Dislodged chest drain

Why Not Others: (a) Leaving the opening lets air enter the chest; (b) Pushing the tube back may cause harm; (d) Walking strains his breathing.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is pushed back into the chest at once.

5-Second Recall: Cover the opening with a sterile dressing and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cover the hole, stop the air.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who has severe diarrhoea for 2 days notes that she feels weak and dizzy on standing. Which level is the MOST likely for the nurse to expect?
option_1: A high blood sugar level
option_2: A high blood potassium level
option_3: A high blood calcium level
option_4: A low blood potassium level
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A low blood potassium level

Clinical Rationale: Severe diarrhoea for 2 days drains salts from the body, so a low blood potassium level is expected with the weakness.

Key Clue: severe diarrhoea with weakness and dizziness

Priority Principle: Potassium loss

Why Not Others: (a) Blood sugar is not the level lost here; (b) Diarrhoea lowers, not raises, potassium; (c) Calcium is not the level lost here.

PGI Exam Trap: A high blood potassium level is expected with diarrhoea.

5-Second Recall: A low blood potassium level is expected.

PNC Exam Pearl: Diarrhoea drains the salts.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of the main parts of breast milk as the feeding goes on. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST parts?
option_1: The rich milk comes FIRST, then the thin milk
option_2: The thin watery milk comes FIRST, then the rich milk
option_3: The same milk comes all through the feed
option_4: Only the watery milk comes out at any feed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The thin watery milk comes FIRST, then the rich milk

Clinical Rationale: In a feed the thin watery milk comes out FIRST to quench the thirst, and the rich milk follows to give the fat and energy.

Key Clue: the parts of breast milk in a feed

Priority Principle: Foremilk and hindmilk

Why Not Others: (a) The rich milk comes later, not at the start; (c) The milk changes through a feed; (d) The watery milk is not the whole of the feed.

PGI Exam Trap: The rich milk is said to come FIRST at a feed.

5-Second Recall: The thin watery milk comes first, then the rich milk.

PNC Exam Pearl: Thin then rich.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who had a large vomit while drowsy notes that his breathing has become noisy. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Turn him to the side and clear the mouth
option_2: Lay him flat and give a drink
option_3: Note it and let him sleep
option_4: Sit him up and give a large meal
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Turn him to the side and clear the mouth

Clinical Rationale: Noisy breathing after a large vomit points to food in the airway, so he is turned to the side and the mouth is cleared at once.

Key Clue: noisy breathing after a large vomit

Priority Principle: Airway obstruction

Why Not Others: (b) Laying him flat and giving a drink risks choking; (c) Letting him sleep misses the danger; (d) A large meal adds to the choking risk.

PGI Exam Trap: He is laid flat and given a large drink.

5-Second Recall: Turn him to the side and clear the mouth.

PNC Exam Pearl: Vomit and noisy breath mean clear the airway.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the stages of a fever is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: A dry warm skin marks the stage when the fever has passed
option_2: A chill with shivering marks the stage when the fever has settled
option_3: Sweating marks the stage when the temperature is climbing
option_4: A chill with shivering marks the stage when the temperature is rising
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A chill with shivering marks the stage when the temperature is rising

Clinical Rationale: A chill with shivering marks the rising stage of a fever, as the body sets its heat higher and feels cold in the meantime.

Key Clue: the stages of a fever

Priority Principle: Stages of fever

Why Not Others: (a) A dry warm skin marks the rising, not the passing, stage; (b) Shivering marks the rising, not the settling stage; (c) Sweating marks the stage of falling temperature.

PGI Exam Trap: Shivering is called the stage when the fever has settled.

5-Second Recall: A chill with shivering marks the rising stage.

PNC Exam Pearl: Shiver first, sweat later.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who is very sad and quiet for 3 weeks notes that she has given away her things and talks of being a burden. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Leave her alone until she asks for help
option_2: Tell her that she has much to live for
option_3: Ask her plainly about thoughts of harming herself
option_4: Give her a job to keep her busy
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Ask her plainly about thoughts of harming herself

Clinical Rationale: Giving away things with talk of being a burden points to a high risk of self harm, so the nurse asks her plainly about her safety.

Key Clue: a woman giving away her things after weeks of sadness

Priority Principle: Risk of self harm

Why Not Others: (a) Leaving her alone misses the danger; (b) Saying she has much to live for does not lower the risk; (d) A busy job does not answer the risk.

PGI Exam Trap: She is left alone until she asks for help.

5-Second Recall: Ask her plainly about thoughts of harming herself.

PNC Exam Pearl: Giving things away means ask about harm.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic is shown a report with a haemoglobin of 8 g/dL at 28 weeks. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Report it and start iron and folic acid
option_2: Tell her that the level is quite normal
option_3: Ask her to walk fast up the stairs each day
option_4: Hold back her iron rich food for now
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Report it and start iron and folic acid

Clinical Rationale: A haemoglobin of 8 g/dL in pregnancy is low, so it is reported and iron with folic acid is started to build the blood.

Key Clue: a haemoglobin of 8 g/dL at 28 weeks

Priority Principle: Anaemia in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (b) The level is not normal at all; (c) Fast walking strains a woman short of blood; (d) Iron rich food is needed, not held back.

PGI Exam Trap: The level is called normal and nothing is done.

5-Second Recall: Report it and start iron and folic acid.

PNC Exam Pearl: 8 g/dL in pregnancy needs iron.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who has diarrhoea and vomiting notes a sunken soft spot and no tears when the child cries. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take?
option_1: Hold back all fluids for a full day
option_2: Give oral rehydration fluid and tell the doctor
option_3: Give plain water in very large amounts
option_4: Wait and check the child in the morning
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give oral rehydration fluid and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A sunken soft spot with no tears points to NOT enough fluid, so oral rehydration fluid is given and the doctor told.

Key Clue: a sunken soft spot with no tears in a child

Priority Principle: Dehydration in a child

Why Not Others: (a) Holding back fluids makes the loss worse; (c) Plain water alone does not replace salts; (d) Waiting a night lets the child worsen.

PGI Exam Trap: All fluids are held back for a full day.

5-Second Recall: Give oral rehydration fluid and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sunken spot, no tears means dried out.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a tracheostomy notes that he is coughing and his lips are turning blue. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give him a drink of water
option_2: Change the ties on the tube
option_3: Suction the tube and give oxygen
option_4: Leave him to rest for a while
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Suction the tube and give oxygen

Clinical Rationale: Coughing with blue lips points to a blocked tracheostomy tube, so the tube is suctioned and oxygen is given at once.

Key Clue: a tracheostomy tube with coughing and blue lips

Priority Principle: Blocked tracheostomy

Why Not Others: (a) A drink may go into the airway; (b) Changing the ties does not clear the tube; (d) Waiting lets the low oxygen worsen.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube ties are changed while the lips are blue.

5-Second Recall: Suction the tube and give oxygen.

PNC Exam Pearl: Blue lips need suction now.

question: A community nurse visiting a family is asked which statement about the cold chain for vaccines is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The vaccines need no care in the summer heat
option_2: The vaccines are kept warm before they are used
option_3: The vaccines are frozen and thawed many times
option_4: The vaccines are kept cool from the place of making to the child
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The vaccines are kept cool from the place of making to the child

Clinical Rationale: The cold chain keeps vaccines cool from the place of making all the way to the child, so that they still work when given.

Key Clue: the cold chain for vaccines

Priority Principle: Cold chain

Why Not Others: (a) Vaccines need careful care in the heat; (b) Warmth spoils the vaccines; (c) Repeated freezing and thawing spoils them.

PGI Exam Trap: The vaccines are kept warm before they are used.

5-Second Recall: Vaccines stay cool from the making to the child.

PNC Exam Pearl: Keep them cool all the way.

question: A nurse caring for an elderly woman on the ward finds the call bell lying on the floor out of her reach. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tie the call bell to the foot of the bed
option_2: Leave it on the floor as she can call out
option_3: Put the call bell back within her reach
option_4: Note it and tell her to be careful
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Put the call bell back within her reach

Clinical Rationale: The call bell is put back within the reach of the woman, so that she can call for help and does NOT try to get up alone.

Key Clue: a call bell out of the reach of an elderly woman

Priority Principle: Patient safety

Why Not Others: (a) A bell at the foot of the bed is hard to reach; (b) She may fall while trying to reach it; (d) A warning does not keep her safe.

PGI Exam Trap: The call bell is left on the floor for her to reach.

5-Second Recall: Put the call bell back within her reach.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bell in reach keeps her safe.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has just returned from an operation notes that he is drowsy and his breathing is slow and shallow. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and check again after an hour
option_2: Give him a warm drink and let him rest
option_3: Raise the bed rails and leave him to sleep
option_4: Wake him and check his airway and breathing
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Wake him and check his airway and breathing

Clinical Rationale: Drowsiness with slow shallow breathing after an operation points to too much sedative drug, so he is woken and his airway checked at once.

Key Clue: drowsiness with slow shallow breathing after an operation

Priority Principle: Sedation after surgery

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting an hour is too long here; (b) A drink while drowsy risks choking; (c) Leaving him to sleep lets the breathing fall.

PGI Exam Trap: He is left asleep and checked after an hour.

5-Second Recall: Wake him and check his airway and breathing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Drowsy and shallow means wake and check.

question: A nurse caring for an infant on the ward who is fed from a bottle notes that the milk runs out of the mouth and the baby turns blue during feeds. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop the feed and check the airway at once
option_2: Give the feed faster to finish it soon
option_3: Lay the baby flat and carry on the feed
option_4: Note it and change the milk brand
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stop the feed and check the airway at once

Clinical Rationale: Milk running out of the mouth with blue colour during feeds points to choking, so the feed is stopped and the airway checked at once.

Key Clue: an infant turning blue during bottle feeds

Priority Principle: Choking during feeds

Why Not Others: (b) A faster feed makes the choking worse; (c) Laying the baby flat adds to the choking; (d) A new brand does not answer the danger.

PGI Exam Trap: The feed is given faster to finish it soon.

5-Second Recall: Stop the feed and check the airway at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Blue during feeds means stop and check.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the small intestine is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is the main place where water is stored
option_2: MOST digestion and absorption takes place in it
option_3: It is the place where bile is made
option_4: It is the place where urine is formed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) MOST digestion and absorption takes place in it

Clinical Rationale: MOST of the digestion of food and the taking in of nutrients happens in the small intestine, along its long coiled length.

Key Clue: the work of the small intestine

Priority Principle: Small intestine

Why Not Others: (a) Water is taken back mostly in the large bowel; (c) Bile is made in the liver, not here; (d) Urine is formed in the kidneys, not here.

PGI Exam Trap: Bile is said to be made in the small intestine.

5-Second Recall: Most digestion and absorption takes place in it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Small gut does the digesting.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward is shown a report with a blood glucose of 40 mg/dL. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Hold all feeds and watch the child
option_2: Give sugar by mouth at once and recheck
option_3: Give a large dose of insulin as ordered
option_4: Note it and check again in the morning
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give sugar by mouth at once and recheck

Clinical Rationale: A blood glucose of 40 mg/dL is low and can harm the brain, so sugar is given by mouth at once and the level rechecked.

Key Clue: a blood glucose of 40 mg/dL in a child

Priority Principle: Low blood sugar

Why Not Others: (a) Holding feeds keeps the sugar low; (c) Insulin would lower the sugar further; (d) Waiting till morning risks the brain.

PGI Exam Trap: Insulin is given for a blood glucose of 40 mg/dL.

5-Second Recall: Give sugar by mouth at once and recheck.

PNC Exam Pearl: 40 mg/dL is low, give sugar.

question: A nurse on the ward is shown a drug label that reads 'Give 500 mg every 6 hours by mouth'. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give the drug by injection instead
option_2: Give the drug once a day instead
option_3: Check the order and give the drug as written
option_4: Double the dose to work faster
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the order and give the drug as written

Clinical Rationale: The label is read against the doctor's order, and the drug is given as written so that the right dose and route are used.

Key Clue: a drug label reading 500 mg every 6 hours

Priority Principle: Drug label check

Why Not Others: (a) The label says by mouth, not by injection; (b) Once a day is not what the label says; (d) Doubling the dose may harm the client.

PGI Exam Trap: The dose is doubled to make the drug work faster.

5-Second Recall: Check the order and give the drug as written.

PNC Exam Pearl: Read the label, match the order.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has just had a chest tube removed notes that he becomes breathless and his wound has a small crackle of air. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give him a hot drink and let him rest
option_2: Ask him to take a deep breath and lie flat
option_3: Leave the site and note it for the round
option_4: Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help

Clinical Rationale: Breathlessness with air leaking from the wound after a chest tube is out points to air entering the chest, so a sterile dressing is pressed on and help called.

Key Clue: a small crackle of air at the wound after a chest tube

Priority Principle: Air leak

Why Not Others: (a) A hot drink does not stop the air leak; (b) Lying flat may worsen his breathing; (c) Leaving the site lets air enter the chest.

PGI Exam Trap: The site is left alone and noted for the round.

5-Second Recall: Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Air at the wound means press and call.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic is asked which statement about a normal pregnancy is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The blood pressure stays much the same as before pregnancy
option_2: The blood pressure rises sharply in every pregnancy
option_3: The blood pressure falls to very low in every pregnancy
option_4: The blood pressure cannot be measured in pregnancy
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The blood pressure stays much the same as before pregnancy

Clinical Rationale: In a normal pregnancy the blood pressure stays much the same as before, and any sharp rise is watched for as a danger sign.

Key Clue: the blood pressure in a normal pregnancy

Priority Principle: Blood pressure in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (b) A sharp rise points to a problem, not the usual; (c) Very low pressure is not the normal rule; (d) Blood pressure is measured at every check.

PGI Exam Trap: The blood pressure is said to rise sharply in every pregnancy.

5-Second Recall: The blood pressure stays much the same as before.

PNC Exam Pearl: Steady pressure is the normal.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about insulin storage is NOT correct.
option_1: Insulin in use is kept in a cool dark place
option_2: Insulin is kept in the freezer to stay fresh
option_3: Insulin is NOT shaken hard before it is drawn
option_4: Insulin is checked for the date before it is used
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Insulin is kept in the freezer to stay fresh

Clinical Rationale: Insulin must never be frozen, as ice destroys it, so keeping it in the freezer is the statement that is wrong.

Key Clue: the correct storage of insulin

Priority Principle: Insulin storage

Why Not Others: (a) A cool dark place is the correct storage; (c) Shaking hard spoils insulin, so it is avoided; (d) Checking the date is correct practice.

PGI Exam Trap: Insulin is kept in the freezer and called fresh.

5-Second Recall: Insulin is not frozen but kept cool.

PNC Exam Pearl: Freezing kills insulin.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a manic client is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: He is given strong coffee to settle him
option_2: He is put in a busy ward with many people
option_3: He is kept in a calm, low noise area with few people
option_4: He is asked to take part in a loud group game
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) He is kept in a calm, low noise area with few people

Clinical Rationale: A manic client is over-active and easily stirred, so he is kept in a calm, low noise area with few people to help him settle.

Key Clue: the care of a manic client

Priority Principle: Manic client care

Why Not Others: (a) Coffee adds to his over-activity; (b) A busy ward stirs him more; (d) A loud game raises his activity.

PGI Exam Trap: He is put in a busy ward with many people to settle him.

5-Second Recall: He is kept in a calm, low noise area with few people.

PNC Exam Pearl: Calm and quiet for mania.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a bed bath to a man. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Wash the back FIRST, then the face, then the arms
option_2: Wash the trunk FIRST, then the face, then the legs
option_3: Wash the legs FIRST, then the face, then the arms
option_4: Wash the face FIRST, then the arms, then the trunk
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Wash the face FIRST, then the arms, then the trunk

Clinical Rationale: The bed bath starts at the face and works down to the arms and trunk, so that the cleanest part is washed with the cleanest water.

Key Clue: the steps for giving a bed bath

Priority Principle: Bed bath order

Why Not Others: (a) The face comes before the back; (b) The clean face is washed before the trunk; (c) The face is washed first of all.

PGI Exam Trap: The legs are washed before the face in this bath.

5-Second Recall: Wash the face first, then the arms, then the trunk.

PNC Exam Pearl: Face, arms, trunk.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a blood transfusion to a woman. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Check the order, check the blood with a second nurse, then start the drip
option_2: Start the drip FIRST and then check the blood
option_3: Check the blood alone, start the drip, then check the order
option_4: Start the drip and check the label during the drip
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check the order, check the blood with a second nurse, then start the drip

Clinical Rationale: The nurse checks the order, checks the blood against the client with a second nurse, and then starts the drip, so that the right blood is given.

Key Clue: the steps for a blood transfusion

Priority Principle: Transfusion order

Why Not Others: (b) The blood is checked before the drip is started; (c) Checking the order comes first of all; (d) The label is checked before the drip starts.

PGI Exam Trap: The drip is started before the blood is checked.

5-Second Recall: Check the order, check the blood, then start the drip.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check order and blood, then drip.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who is given a pain killer by drip is asked which effect is the MOST important to watch.
option_1: Slow shallow breathing with a falling pulse oxygen level
option_2: A rise in the child's body temperature
option_3: A loud cry with a lot of movement
option_4: A dry mouth with strong thirst
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Slow shallow breathing with a falling pulse oxygen level

Clinical Rationale: A strong pain killer by drip can slow the breathing of a child, so slow shallow breathing with a falling oxygen level is watched with care.

Key Clue: the effects of a pain killer by drip in a child

Priority Principle: Opioid in children

Why Not Others: (b) A rise in temperature is not the main effect; (c) A loud cry is not the danger here; (d) A dry mouth is a small effect.

PGI Exam Trap: A rise in temperature is watched as the main drug effect.

5-Second Recall: Slow shallow breathing with a falling oxygen level is watched.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watch the breath after the drug.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward notes that his blood potassium is 6.5 mmol/L. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give him a drink rich in potassium
option_2: Stop any potassium and tell the doctor at once
option_3: Wait and recheck the level next week
option_4: Ask him to eat more bananas and dates
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop any potassium and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A blood potassium of 6.5 mmol/L is dangerously high and can stop the heart, so potassium is stopped and the doctor told.

Key Clue: a blood potassium of 6.5 mmol/L

Priority Principle: Hyperkalaemia

Why Not Others: (a) A potassium drink would raise it further; (c) Waiting a week risks the heart; (d) Bananas and dates add more potassium.

PGI Exam Trap: A drink rich in potassium is given at this level.

5-Second Recall: Stop any potassium and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: 6.5 is high, hold the potassium.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked which statement about a panic attack is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Leave her alone until the attack passes
option_2: Tell her to breathe fast into a paper bag
option_3: Stay with her and speak in a calm, quiet voice
option_4: Hold her arms to keep her very still
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stay with her and speak in a calm, quiet voice

Clinical Rationale: Staying with the woman and speaking calmly helps her feel safe and brings the panic down.

Key Clue: the care of a woman during a panic attack

Priority Principle: Panic attack

Why Not Others: (a) Leaving her alone adds to the fear; (b) Fast breathing into a bag is not advised; (d) Holding her arms adds to the panic.

PGI Exam Trap: The woman is left alone until the attack passes.

5-Second Recall: Stay with her and speak in a calm voice.

PNC Exam Pearl: Stay calm and stay near.

question: A community nurse visits a family whose 2-year-old child has a high fever with a rash that does NOT fade when pressed. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell the family that it is a simple cold
option_2: Give a home remedy and wait
option_3: Ask the family to come back next month
option_4: Send the child to hospital at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the child to hospital at once

Clinical Rationale: A rash that does NOT fade when pressed with a high fever points to a serious illness, so the child is sent to hospital at once.

Key Clue: a high fever with a rash that does NOT fade

Priority Principle: Serious febrile illness

Why Not Others: (a) A simple cold does not cause this rash; (b) A home remedy delays the treatment; (c) A month later is far too late.

PGI Exam Trap: A home remedy is given and the family waits.

5-Second Recall: Send the child to hospital at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: A rash that will not fade means go now.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has been on a drip for 2 days notes that his hand is puffed and cool at the drip site. Which finding is the MOST likely for the nurse to expect?
option_1: The fluid has stopped entering the body
option_2: The fluid has gone into the vein as wanted
option_3: The fluid has gone into the lungs instead
option_4: The fluid has gone into the tissue around the vein
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The fluid has gone into the tissue around the vein

Clinical Rationale: A puffed cool hand at a drip site points to the fluid leaking into the tissue around the vein, which is known as extravasation.

Key Clue: a puffed cool hand at a drip site

Priority Principle: Extravasation

Why Not Others: (a) The fluid is flowing, but in the wrong place; (b) Into the vein is the wanted path, not this; (c) Fluid in the lungs gives breathlessness.

PGI Exam Trap: The fluid is said to have gone into the vein as wanted.

5-Second Recall: The fluid has leaked into the tissue around the vein.

PNC Exam Pearl: Puffed cool hand means the drip has slipped.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who takes digoxin is shown a report with a digoxin level of 2.6 ng/mL. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Double the next dose as ordered
option_2: Give the next dose early to settle her
option_3: Hold the drug and tell the doctor at once
option_4: Note it and plan the dose for tomorrow
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Hold the drug and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A digoxin level of 2.6 ng/mL is above the safe range, so the drug is held and the doctor told at once to avoid harm.

Key Clue: a digoxin level of 2.6 ng/mL

Priority Principle: Digoxin toxicity

Why Not Others: (a) Doubling the dose is dangerous here; (b) An early dose adds to the toxic level; (d) Waiting risks serious heart effects.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose is doubled at a level of 2.6 ng/mL.

5-Second Recall: Hold the drug and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Above 2.0 means hold the digoxin.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has been on bed rest for 5 days notes a swollen painful calf on one side. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Massage the calf to ease the pain
option_2: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once
option_3: Ask him to walk fast to the bathroom
option_4: Put a warm pack on and then wait
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A swollen painful calf on one side after days in bed points to a deep vein clot, so the leg is kept still and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: a swollen painful calf after days in bed

Priority Principle: Deep vein thrombosis

Why Not Others: (a) Massage may break off the clot; (c) Fast walking may move the clot to the lungs; (d) A warm pack does not treat the danger.

PGI Exam Trap: The calf is massaged to ease the pain.

5-Second Recall: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen calf after bed rest means a clot.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about giving a drug by the under the tongue route is NOT correct.
option_1: The tablet is swallowed with a large drink of water
option_2: The tablet is kept under the tongue until it dissolves
option_3: The client is asked NOT to eat while it dissolves
option_4: The tablet is NOT chewed before it dissolves
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The tablet is swallowed with a large drink of water

Clinical Rationale: A tablet under the tongue is meant to dissolve there and pass into the blood, so swallowing it with water is the statement that is wrong.

Key Clue: the correct use of the under the tongue route

Priority Principle: Sublingual route

Why Not Others: (b) Keeping it under the tongue is correct; (c) Not eating while it dissolves is correct; (d) Not chewing it is correct.

PGI Exam Trap: The tablet is swallowed with water and still called sublingual.

5-Second Recall: The tablet is kept under the tongue until it dissolves.

PNC Exam Pearl: Under the tongue, let it dissolve.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to insert a urinary catheter in a woman. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Insert the catheter without cleaning the area
option_2: Insert the catheter FIRST and then clean the area
option_3: Clean the area, insert the catheter, then clean the hands
option_4: Clean the hands, clean the area, then insert the catheter
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Clean the hands, clean the area, then insert the catheter

Clinical Rationale: The nurse cleans the hands, cleans the area, and then inserts the catheter, so that germs are NOT carried into the bladder.

Key Clue: the steps for inserting a urinary catheter

Priority Principle: Catheter order

Why Not Others: (a) The area is always cleaned before the tube; (b) The area is cleaned before the catheter is passed; (c) Cleaning the hands comes first of all.

PGI Exam Trap: The catheter is inserted without cleaning the area.

5-Second Recall: Clean the hands, clean the area, then insert the catheter.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands, clean area, then pass.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who has croup notes a harsh noise when the child breathes in and out. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give the child a large meal at once
option_2: Ask the child to cry as loudly as possible
option_3: Keep the child calm and give humidified oxygen
option_4: Leave the child alone to sleep
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the child calm and give humidified oxygen

Clinical Rationale: A harsh noise on breathing in and out in croup points to a narrow airway, so the child is kept calm and given humidified oxygen.

Key Clue: a harsh noise on breathing in croup

Priority Principle: Croup

Why Not Others: (a) A large meal may make the breathing worse; (b) Crying tightens the narrow airway; (d) Leaving the child alone misses the distress.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is asked to cry as loudly as possible.

5-Second Recall: Keep the child calm and give humidified oxygen.

PNC Exam Pearl: Calm the child, moist the air.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who had a stroke 2 days ago notes that she suddenly becomes drowsy and one pupil is larger than the other. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give her a drink and let her rest
option_2: Call for help and check her breathing
option_3: Ask her to walk to test her strength
option_4: Note it and wait for the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Call for help and check her breathing

Clinical Rationale: Drowsiness with one pupil larger than the other after a stroke points to swelling in the brain, so help is called and her breathing checked at once.

Key Clue: one pupil larger than the other after a stroke

Priority Principle: Raised brain pressure

Why Not Others: (a) A drink while drowsy risks choking; (c) Walking is unsafe with this sign; (d) Waiting for the round misses the danger.

PGI Exam Trap: The sign is noted and the ward round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Call for help and check her breathing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Big pupil after a stroke means call for help.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes warfarin is asked about his care. Which finding is the MOST important for the nurse to report?
option_1: Bleeding gums with dark stools
option_2: A good appetite at all meals
option_3: A calm mood during the day
option_4: A steady pulse of 80 bpm
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Bleeding gums with dark stools

Clinical Rationale: Warfarin thins the blood, so bleeding gums with dark stools point to too much drug and are reported at once.

Key Clue: bleeding gums with dark stools on warfarin

Priority Principle: Warfarin overdose

Why Not Others: (b) A good appetite is reassuring; (c) A calm mood is not a bleeding sign; (d) A steady pulse of 80 bpm is normal.

PGI Exam Trap: A steady pulse of 80 bpm is reported as bleeding.

5-Second Recall: Bleeding gums with dark stools are reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Gums bleed, warfarin is too much.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has taken little food for 5 days is planning his care. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Check his weight and ask the dietitian to see him
option_2: Give him a very large meal at once
option_3: Wait for him to ask for food himself
option_4: Give him strong coffee to stir his hunger
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check his weight and ask the dietitian to see him

Clinical Rationale: After 5 days without food the man needs proper nourishment, so his weight is checked and the dietitian is asked to plan a build-up diet.

Key Clue: a man who has taken little food for 5 days

Priority Principle: Poor intake

Why Not Others: (b) A very large meal after starvation may harm him; (c) Waiting lets him become weaker; (d) Coffee does not give nourishment.

PGI Exam Trap: He is given a very large meal at once.

5-Second Recall: Check his weight and ask the dietitian to see him.

PNC Exam Pearl: Days without food need a diet plan.

question: A community nurse visits a village where many children have red sore eyes with a yellow discharge. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give each child a pair of dark glasses and send them home
option_2: Tell the families that the illness is NOT spread by contact
option_3: Ask the families to keep the children indoors for a month
option_4: Teach hand and face washing and treat the affected children
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Teach hand and face washing and treat the affected children

Clinical Rationale: Red sore eyes with a yellow discharge point to a spread of infection by contact, so washing of hands and face is taught and the children are treated.

Key Clue: many children with red sore eyes and discharge

Priority Principle: Eye infection spread

Why Not Others: (a) Dark glasses do not treat the infection; (b) The illness is spread by contact, so this is false; (c) A month indoors does not stop the spread.

PGI Exam Trap: The families are told that the illness is NOT spread by contact.

5-Second Recall: Teach hand and face washing and treat the affected children.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sore red eyes mean clean hands and faces.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes lithium is asked which finding is the MOST important to report.
option_1: A good appetite at all meals
option_2: A steady mood over the past week
option_3: A coarse tremor with vomiting and loose stools
option_4: A calm sleep through the night
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A coarse tremor with vomiting and loose stools

Clinical Rationale: A coarse tremor with vomiting and loose stools on lithium points to a level that has gone too high, so it is reported at once.

Key Clue: a coarse tremor with vomiting on lithium

Priority Principle: Lithium toxicity

Why Not Others: (a) A good appetite is reassuring; (b) A steady mood is the aim of the drug; (d) Calm sleep is not a sign of danger.

PGI Exam Trap: A steady mood is reported as the sign of too much lithium.

5-Second Recall: A coarse tremor with vomiting is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Shaky and sick means lithium is high.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is shown a monitor strip with tall peaked waves and a slow rate of 45 bpm. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give him a drink rich in potassium
option_2: Check his drugs and tell the doctor at once
option_3: Ask him to walk to test the rhythm
option_4: Note the strip for the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check his drugs and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: Tall peaked waves with a slow rate point to a high blood potassium, so his drugs are checked and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: tall peaked waves with a slow rate of 45 bpm

Priority Principle: Hyperkalaemia on the monitor

Why Not Others: (a) A potassium drink would raise the level more; (c) Walking may worsen the slow rhythm; (d) Waiting for the round risks the heart.

PGI Exam Trap: The tall strips are noted for the ward round.

5-Second Recall: Check his drugs and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tall peaked waves mean a high potassium.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a nasogastric tube left in place is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The feed is given fast while the man lies flat
option_2: The tube is left without any check at all
option_3: The position of the tube is checked before every feed
option_4: The tube is pulled out by the man himself
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The position of the tube is checked before every feed

Clinical Rationale: The position of a nasogastric tube is checked before every feed, so that the feed does NOT go into the airway.

Key Clue: the care of a nasogastric tube in place

Priority Principle: Nasogastric tube

Why Not Others: (a) A fast feed with the man flat may choke him; (b) The tube is checked before each feed; (d) The tube is not pulled out by the man.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is left in place with no check before the feed.

5-Second Recall: The position of the tube is checked before every feed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the tube, then feed.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward is asked which sign is the MOST important warning of a blocked airway in a young child.
option_1: A wet nappy every hour through the day
option_2: A harsh noise on breathing in with a hoarse cry
option_3: A good appetite at all the meal times
option_4: Pink lips with warm hands and feet
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A harsh noise on breathing in with a hoarse cry

Clinical Rationale: A harsh noise on breathing in with a hoarse cry is a strong warning that air is NOT moving freely in a young child.

Key Clue: the warning signs of a blocked airway in a child

Priority Principle: Airway obstruction

Why Not Others: (a) A wet nappy every hour is a good sign; (c) A good appetite is reassuring; (d) Pink lips with warm hands are reassuring.

PGI Exam Trap: A wet nappy every hour is called a blocked airway.

5-Second Recall: A harsh noise on breathing in is the warning.

PNC Exam Pearl: Noisy in-breath means a tight airway.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps in the chain of survival for a man who has collapsed. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Check for a response, call for help, then start chest presses
option_2: Start chest presses FIRST and then call for help
option_3: Call for help, start chest presses, then check for a response
option_4: Start chest presses without checking for a response
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check for a response, call for help, then start chest presses

Clinical Rationale: The nurse checks for a response, calls for help, and then starts chest presses, so that a stopped heart is treated without delay.

Key Clue: the FIRST steps of the chain of survival

Priority Principle: Cardiac arrest order

Why Not Others: (b) Help is called before the chest presses begin; (c) Checking for a response comes first of all; (d) A response is checked before pressing.

PGI Exam Trap: Chest presses are started without checking for a response.

5-Second Recall: Check for a response, call for help, then start chest presses.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check, call, then press.

question: A community nurse is asked which action is the MOST appropriate for a child who is given a vaccine and then has a mild fever.
option_1: Tell the family that the fever will never settle
option_2: Give a strong pain killer by injection at once
option_3: Ask the family to stop all further vaccines
option_4: Give paracetamol as ordered and advise plenty of fluids
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give paracetamol as ordered and advise plenty of fluids

Clinical Rationale: A mild fever after a vaccine is a common and short effect, so paracetamol as ordered with plenty of fluids is the right care.

Key Clue: a mild fever after a vaccine

Priority Principle: Vaccine reaction

Why Not Others: (a) The fever settles on its own soon; (b) A strong pain killer by injection is not needed; (c) Further vaccines are still needed.

PGI Exam Trap: All further vaccines are stopped for a mild fever.

5-Second Recall: Give paracetamol as ordered and advise plenty of fluids.

PNC Exam Pearl: Mild fever after a shot means simple care.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has mild asthma is asked which action is the MOST appropriate to help him breathe more easily.
option_1: Ask him to run up the stairs to test the lungs
option_2: Ask him to lie flat and take deep rest
option_3: Give him a large hot meal at once
option_4: Help him to sit upright and use his inhaler
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Help him to sit upright and use his inhaler

Clinical Rationale: Sitting upright with the help of an inhaler opens the airway in asthma, so breathing becomes easier for the man.

Key Clue: mild asthma with difficulty in breathing

Priority Principle: Asthma care

Why Not Others: (a) Running strains the tight airway; (b) Lying flat makes the breathing harder; (c) A heavy meal presses on the chest.

PGI Exam Trap: He is asked to lie flat and take deep rest.

5-Second Recall: Help him to sit upright and use his inhaler.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sit up, inhale, breathe easy.

question: A community nurse visiting a family is asked which statement about the management of a person with tuberculosis at home is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The drugs are taken daily for the full course without a break
option_2: The drugs are taken for a week and then stopped
option_3: The drugs are shared with the family members
option_4: The drugs are taken for a month and then paused
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The drugs are taken daily for the full course without a break

Clinical Rationale: Tuberculosis drugs must be taken daily for the full course without a break, so that the germs are killed and do NOT become resistant.

Key Clue: the management of tuberculosis at home

Priority Principle: Tuberculosis treatment

Why Not Others: (b) A week of drugs leaves the germs alive; (c) Drugs are not shared with others; (d) Pausing lets the germs grow back.

PGI Exam Trap: The drugs are shared with the family members.

5-Second Recall: The drugs are taken daily for the full course.

PNC Exam Pearl: Full course, every day, no break.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has loose stools after a course of antibiotics is asked which action is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Stop all fluids and give a strong pain killer
option_2: Collect a stool sample and start the care for his skin
option_3: Give him a hot meal with a lot of spice
option_4: Ask the family to take him home at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Collect a stool sample and start the care for his skin

Clinical Rationale: Loose stools after antibiotics point to a gut infection, so a stool sample is collected and the skin around him is cared for to prevent sores.

Key Clue: loose stools after a course of antibiotics

Priority Principle: Antibiotic associated diarrhoea

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping fluids may dry him out; (c) Spicy food may make the stools worse; (d) Taking him home delays his care.

PGI Exam Trap: All fluids are stopped and a pain killer is given.

5-Second Recall: Collect a stool sample and care for his skin.

PNC Exam Pearl: Antibiotics and loose stools mean send a sample.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has fallen and hurt his arm notes that the arm is bent the wrong way. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask him to bend the arm to test it
option_2: Try to straighten the arm at once
option_3: Keep the arm still and call for help
option_4: Leave the arm and note it for the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the arm still and call for help

Clinical Rationale: An arm bent the wrong way after a fall points to a broken bone, so it is kept still and help is called rather than moved.

Key Clue: an arm bent the wrong way after a fall

Priority Principle: Fracture care

Why Not Others: (a) Bending it to test adds to the damage; (b) Straightening the arm may cause more harm; (d) Waiting leaves the broken arm unmoved but unhelped.

PGI Exam Trap: The arm is straightened at once to test it.

5-Second Recall: Keep the arm still and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Wrong bend means keep it still.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the labour room who is given oxytocin notes that her pains last too long with no rest between. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Speed up the oxytocin to finish the birth
option_2: Stop the oxytocin and call the doctor
option_3: Ask her to walk about the room
option_4: Note it and wait for the next pain
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the oxytocin and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Oxytocin can drive the pains so hard that the womb is never at rest, which harms the baby, so the drug is stopped and the doctor called.

Key Clue: pains with no rest between after oxytocin

Priority Principle: Excess oxytocin

Why Not Others: (a) A faster drip makes the pains harder; (c) Walking does not ease the drive of the drug; (d) Waiting lets the baby be harmed.

PGI Exam Trap: The oxytocin is speeded up to finish the birth.

5-Second Recall: Stop the oxytocin and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: No rest between pains means stop the drug.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward who takes phenytoin is asked which finding is the MOST important to report.
option_1: A calm mood during the day
option_2: A good appetite at all the meals
option_3: Unsteady walking with a coarse tremor
option_4: A steady pulse with warm hands
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Unsteady walking with a coarse tremor

Clinical Rationale: Unsteady walking with a coarse tremor on phenytoin points to a level that has gone too high, so it is reported at once.

Key Clue: unsteady walking with a tremor on phenytoin

Priority Principle: Phenytoin toxicity

Why Not Others: (a) A calm mood is not a drug warning; (b) A good appetite is reassuring; (d) A steady pulse is normal.

PGI Exam Trap: A good appetite is reported as too much phenytoin.

5-Second Recall: Unsteady walking with a coarse tremor is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Unsteady and shaky means phenytoin is high.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has just returned from a thyroid operation notes a swelling at the neck and a change in his voice. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it for the next ward round
option_2: Give him a cold drink at once
option_3: Ask him to lie flat and sleep
option_4: Keep the airway free and call the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep the airway free and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A swelling at the neck with a changed voice after thyroid surgery points to bleeding that can block the airway, so the airway is kept free and the doctor called.

Key Clue: a neck swelling after thyroid surgery

Priority Principle: Airway risk after thyroid surgery

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting risks a blocked airway; (b) A cold drink does not free the airway; (c) Lying flat may block the breathing.

PGI Exam Trap: The swelling is noted for the next ward round.

5-Second Recall: Keep the airway free and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Neck swelling after thyroid blocks the airway.

question: A nurse caring for an elderly man on the ward notes that he is confused and his skin is dry and warm. Which finding is the MOST important for the nurse to check?
option_1: His fluid intake and urine output
option_2: The colour of his eyes and nails
option_3: The brand of his walking stick
option_4: The size of his room and bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) His fluid intake and urine output

Clinical Rationale: Confusion with dry warm skin in an elderly man points to NOT enough fluid, so his intake and urine output are checked at once.

Key Clue: confusion with dry warm skin in an elderly man

Priority Principle: Dehydration

Why Not Others: (b) Eye and nail colour do not show fluid loss; (c) A walking stick does not show fluid loss; (d) The room size is not a fluid check.

PGI Exam Trap: The brand of his walking stick is checked for fluid loss.

5-Second Recall: His fluid intake and urine output are checked.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry, warm and confused means short of fluid.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes a steroid drug every day is asked about stopping it. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It has no effect on the body at all
option_2: It is safe to stop it all in one day
option_3: It can be doubled without telling the doctor
option_4: It is reduced slowly over days and never stopped at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It is reduced slowly over days and never stopped at once

Clinical Rationale: Long term steroids stop the body making its own, so the dose is reduced slowly and never stopped in one day.

Key Clue: stopping a steroid drug taken every day

Priority Principle: Steroid withdrawal

Why Not Others: (a) Steroids act on many body systems; (b) Stopping in one day can cause a crisis; (c) The dose is not doubled without a doctor.

PGI Exam Trap: A daily steroid is stopped safely all in one day.

5-Second Recall: It is reduced slowly and never stopped at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Taper the steroid, never stop it.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a heavy chest infection notes that his breathing is fast and his fingertips look blue. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give oxygen and call the doctor at once
option_2: Ask him to walk to the bathroom
option_3: Give him a large meal to build strength
option_4: Note it and check again after an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give oxygen and call the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: Fast breathing with blue fingertips in a chest infection points to falling oxygen, so oxygen is given and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: fast breathing with blue fingertips in a chest infection

Priority Principle: Low oxygen

Why Not Others: (b) Walking uses more oxygen; (c) A large meal does not help the breathing; (d) Waiting an hour risks his life.

PGI Exam Trap: He is asked to walk to the bathroom to test his breathing.

5-Second Recall: Give oxygen and call the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Blue fingertips mean oxygen now.

question: A community nurse finds that 60 percent of the children in a village are NOT fully immunised. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell the families that they are at fault
option_2: Plan a vaccination camp in the village
option_3: Wait for the families to come to the clinic
option_4: Set the records aside and take no action
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Plan a vaccination camp in the village

Clinical Rationale: With 60 percent of children NOT fully immunised, the nurse plans a vaccination camp so that the missed doses are given close to home.

Key Clue: 60 percent of children NOT fully immunised

Priority Principle: Low immunisation coverage

Why Not Others: (a) Blaming the families does not raise coverage; (c) Waiting for them to come delays the work; (d) Setting the records aside ignores the gap.

PGI Exam Trap: The records are set aside with no action taken.

5-Second Recall: Plan a vaccination camp in the village.

PNC Exam Pearl: Missed doses mean go to the village.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a wound drain after surgery is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The drain is taken out by the nurse alone
option_2: The drain is flushed with water each day
option_3: The amount and colour of the fluid are measured and written down
option_4: The fluid is kept off the chart
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The amount and colour of the fluid are measured and written down

Clinical Rationale: The amount and colour of the fluid from a wound drain are measured and written down, so that bleeding or infection is seen early.

Key Clue: the care of a wound drain after surgery

Priority Principle: Wound drain

Why Not Others: (a) A doctor removes the drain; (b) A drain is not flushed with water; (d) The fluid is always written on the chart.

PGI Exam Trap: The drain fluid is kept off the chart.

5-Second Recall: Measure and write down the amount and colour.

PNC Exam Pearl: Measure the drain, write it down.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the normal colour of urine is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is pale yellow and clear
option_2: It is dark brown and cloudy
option_3: It is red with small clots
option_4: It is green with a strong smell
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It is pale yellow and clear

Clinical Rationale: Normal urine is pale yellow and clear, which shows the man is taking enough fluid and his kidneys are working well.

Key Clue: the normal colour of urine

Priority Principle: Urine colour

Why Not Others: (b) Dark brown cloudy urine points to a problem; (c) Red urine with clots points to bleeding; (d) Green smelly urine points to infection.

PGI Exam Trap: Dark brown cloudy urine is called normal.

5-Second Recall: It is pale yellow and clear.

PNC Exam Pearl: Pale and clear is the normal.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the labour room listens to the baby's heart and counts 100 beats per minute between pains. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Note it and check again next hour
option_2: Tell her that the reading is quite normal
option_3: Ask her to walk about the labour room
option_4: Report it and turn her on her left side
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Report it and turn her on her left side

Clinical Rationale: A baby's heart rate of 100 beats per minute is below the normal range, so it is reported and the woman turned on her left side to improve the flow.

Key Clue: a baby heart rate of 100 bpm between pains

Priority Principle: Low baby heart rate

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting an hour risks the baby; (b) The reading is below the normal range; (c) Walking may lower the flow further.

PGI Exam Trap: The reading of 100 bpm is called normal.

5-Second Recall: Report it and turn her on her left side.

PNC Exam Pearl: 100 bpm is low, turn her left.

question: A community nurse visits a home where a man with a long term illness has a deep wound with a bad smell. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Leave the wound covered for a full month
option_2: Tell the family that the wound is quite normal
option_3: Assess the wound and clean it with the right dressing
option_4: Ask the family to stop all care at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Assess the wound and clean it with the right dressing

Clinical Rationale: A deep smelly wound needs proper care, so the nurse assesses it and cleans it with a dressing chosen for the wound.

Key Clue: a deep smelly wound at home

Priority Principle: Wound care at home

Why Not Others: (a) A month without care lets it worsen; (b) A smelly deep wound is not normal; (d) Stopping care leaves the wound untreated.

PGI Exam Trap: The wound is left covered for a full month.

5-Second Recall: Assess the wound and clean it with the right dressing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Smelly wound needs a proper dressing.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic is asked which statement about the FIRST visit in pregnancy is NOT correct.
option_1: Her weight and blood pressure are recorded
option_2: The woman is asked to skip all further visits
option_3: Her blood and urine are tested
option_4: She is given iron and folic acid tablets
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The woman is asked to skip all further visits

Clinical Rationale: The FIRST visit begins proper antenatal care, so asking the woman to skip all further visits is the statement that is wrong.
