Key Clue: the care given at the FIRST antenatal visit

Priority Principle: Antenatal visits

Why Not Others: (a) Recording weight and pressure is correct; (c) Testing blood and urine is correct; (d) Giving iron and folic acid is correct.

PGI Exam Trap: The woman is asked to skip all further visits and this is called good care.

5-Second Recall: She is asked to come for regular visits, not to skip them.

PNC Exam Pearl: Regular visits, not skipping.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward sees a colleague share a woman's private details with a person who is NOT in the care team. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell other patients about it
option_2: Ignore it as a small matter
option_3: Report the breach to the senior nurse
option_4: Blame the colleague in front of all
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report the breach to the senior nurse

Clinical Rationale: Patient details are private, so a breach is reported to the senior nurse, who can put it right in the proper way.

Key Clue: a colleague who shares private details

Priority Principle: Confidentiality breach

Why Not Others: (a) Telling others spreads the breach; (b) Ignoring it lets the breach go on; (d) Public blame is not the proper way.

PGI Exam Trap: The breach is ignored as a small matter.

5-Second Recall: Report the breach to the senior nurse.

PNC Exam Pearl: A privacy breach is reported.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is on a drip notes that the site is swollen and painful and the drip has slowed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Speed up the drip to clear the swelling
option_2: Stop the drip and restart it in the other arm
option_3: Ask him to move his arm to free the flow
option_4: Note it and check the drip in an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the drip and restart it in the other arm

Clinical Rationale: A swollen painful drip site with a slow flow points to the fluid going into the tissue, so the drip is stopped and restarted in the other arm.

Key Clue: a swollen painful drip site with a slow flow

Priority Principle: Infiltration

Why Not Others: (a) Speeding up the drip makes the swelling worse; (c) Moving the arm does not free the flow; (d) Waiting an hour lets the tissue swell more.

PGI Exam Trap: The drip is speeded up to clear the swelling.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drip and restart it in the other arm.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen drip site means stop and move it.

question: A community nurse visits a village where several people have severe watery stools with quick drying of the body. Which action is the MOST important for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Start oral rehydration for the sick ones at once
option_2: Wait for the doctor to visit the next day
option_3: Advise the families to stop all fluids
option_4: Give a strong pain killer to each person
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Start oral rehydration for the sick ones at once

Clinical Rationale: Severe watery stools with quick drying point to a spread of cholera, so oral rehydration is started at once to save the sick.

Key Clue: severe watery stools with quick drying in a village

Priority Principle: Cholera outbreak

Why Not Others: (b) Waiting a day risks many deaths; (c) Stopping fluids makes the drying worse; (d) A pain killer does not replace the lost fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: All fluids are stopped for the sick people.

5-Second Recall: Start oral rehydration for the sick ones at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watery stools mean fluids now.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is dying asks for more of a pain killer when the ordered dose is small. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop all pain killers to keep him safe
option_2: Give him a double dose without telling anyone
option_3: Tell him that he must bear the pain
option_4: Report his pain and ask the doctor to review the dose
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Report his pain and ask the doctor to review the dose

Clinical Rationale: A dying man in pain needs proper relief, so his pain is reported and the doctor asked to review the dose within the rules.

Key Clue: a dying man in pain with a small ordered dose

Priority Principle: Pain relief at the end of life

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping all pain killers leaves him in pain; (b) A double dose without an order is unsafe; (c) Asking him to bear the pain is unkind and wrong.

PGI Exam Trap: A double dose is given without telling anyone.

5-Second Recall: Report his pain and ask the doctor to review the dose.

PNC Exam Pearl: Report the pain, review the dose.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is started on a new antibiotic by drip develops a swollen face and a tight chest. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Finish the dose and then report
option_2: Slow the drip and watch him
option_3: Give him a warm drink of milk
option_4: Stop the drip and call the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Stop the drip and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A swollen face with a tight chest during a new antibiotic drip points to a severe allergy, so the drip is stopped and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: a swollen face with a tight chest during a drip

Priority Principle: Anaphylaxis

Why Not Others: (a) Finishing the dose is dangerous here; (b) Slowing the drip still feeds the allergy; (c) A warm drink does not treat this.

PGI Exam Trap: The dose is finished and then reported.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drip and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen face on a drip means stop it.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a crush injury to the leg notes that his urine is dark and his pulse is rising. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask him to walk to test the leg
option_2: Hold his fluids to rest the kidneys
option_3: Report it and give fluids as ordered
option_4: Note it and wait for the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report it and give fluids as ordered

Clinical Rationale: Dark urine with a rising pulse after a crush injury points to muscle breakdown harming the kidneys, so it is reported and fluids are given.

Key Clue: dark urine with a rising pulse after a crush injury

Priority Principle: Rhabdomyolysis

Why Not Others: (a) Walking strains the injured leg; (b) Holding fluids lets the kidneys be harmed more; (d) Waiting for the round risks the kidneys.

PGI Exam Trap: Fluids are held back to rest the kidneys.

5-Second Recall: Report it and give fluids as ordered.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dark urine after a crush means give fluids.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a colostomy is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The stoma is black and dry and sinks inside
option_2: The stoma is red and moist and sits on the skin
option_3: The stoma is pale and wet and smells foul
option_4: The stoma is blue and hard and lies flat
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The stoma is red and moist and sits on the skin

Clinical Rationale: A healthy stoma is red and moist and sits on the skin, which shows that the bowel has a good blood supply.

Key Clue: the normal look of a colostomy stoma

Priority Principle: Colostomy stoma

Why Not Others: (a) A black dry stoma shows poor blood supply; (c) A pale foul stoma points to a problem; (d) A blue hard flat stoma is not healthy.

PGI Exam Trap: A black dry stoma is called normal.

5-Second Recall: The stoma is red and moist and sits on the skin.

PNC Exam Pearl: Red and moist is healthy.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is given a strong pain killer notes that his breathing has become slow and shallow. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Stop the drug and call the doctor at once
option_2: Give the next dose early to settle him
option_3: Ask him to walk to deepen his breathing
option_4: Note it and check again in an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stop the drug and call the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A strong pain killer can slow the breathing, so when it becomes slow and shallow the drug is stopped and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: slow shallow breathing after a strong pain killer

Priority Principle: Opioid induced slow breathing

Why Not Others: (b) An early dose deepens the slow breathing; (c) Walking while drowsy is unsafe; (d) Waiting an hour risks his life.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose is given early to settle him.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drug and call the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Slow breath after a pain killer means stop.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who takes phenytoin is shown a report with a level of 25 mcg/mL. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Hold the drug and tell the doctor at once
option_2: Give the next dose early as ordered
option_3: Tell her that the level is quite normal
option_4: Double the next dose to work faster
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Hold the drug and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A phenytoin level of 25 mcg/mL is above the safe range of 10 to 20, so the drug is held and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: a phenytoin level of 25 mcg/mL

Priority Principle: Phenytoin toxicity

Why Not Others: (b) An early dose adds to the high level; (c) The level is above the safe range; (d) Doubling the dose is dangerous.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose is doubled at a level of 25 mcg/mL.

5-Second Recall: Hold the drug and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Above 20 means hold the phenytoin.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse manager on the ward hears that a family is unhappy about how their father was moved in his bed. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Set the complaint aside and move on
option_2: Deny that anything at all went wrong
option_3: Blame the junior nurse in the open
option_4: Listen to the family and note their concern
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Listen to the family and note their concern

Clinical Rationale: The manager listens to the family and notes the concern FIRST, so that the true picture is known before any answer is given.

Key Clue: a family unhappy about a patient being moved

Priority Principle: Complaint handling

Why Not Others: (a) Setting it aside leaves the family unheard; (b) A flat denial does not answer the concern; (c) Open blame breaks the team and helps no one.

PGI Exam Trap: The complaint is set aside and the manager moves on.

5-Second Recall: Listen to the family and note their concern.

PNC Exam Pearl: Hear the concern first.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a normal adult pulse is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is regular and about 160 beats a minute
option_2: It is irregular and about 40 beats a minute
option_3: It is regular and between 60 and 100 beats a minute
option_4: It is irregular and about 200 beats a minute
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It is regular and between 60 and 100 beats a minute

Clinical Rationale: A normal adult pulse is regular and falls between 60 and 100 beats a minute, which shows the heart is working well.

Key Clue: the normal adult pulse

Priority Principle: Normal pulse

Why Not Others: (a) A pulse of about 160 is too fast; (b) A pulse of about 40 is too slow; (d) A pulse of about 200 is far too fast.

PGI Exam Trap: A pulse of 160 beats a minute is called normal.

5-Second Recall: It is regular and between 60 and 100 beats a minute.

PNC Exam Pearl: Regular and 60 to 100.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has an ileostomy is asked which statement about his diet is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: He is asked to skip all fluids through the day
option_2: He is asked to chew well and drink enough fluid
option_3: He is given very large meals three times a day
option_4: He is asked to eat only dry food for a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) He is asked to chew well and drink enough fluid

Clinical Rationale: A man with an ileostomy loses fluid and salts, so he is asked to chew well and drink enough fluid through the day.

Key Clue: the diet of a man with an ileostomy

Priority Principle: Ileostomy diet

Why Not Others: (a) Skipping fluids risks drying him out; (c) Very large meals may cause loose output; (d) Dry food alone does not give enough fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: He is asked to skip all fluids through the day.

5-Second Recall: He is asked to chew well and drink enough fluid.

PNC Exam Pearl: Chew well, drink enough.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who has severe burns notes that her urine output has fallen and her pulse is rising. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Hold her fluids to reduce the swelling
option_2: Give fluids as ordered and tell the doctor
option_3: Ask her to walk to improve the flow
option_4: Note it and check again in an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give fluids as ordered and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Falling urine output with a rising pulse after severe burns points to NOT enough fluid in the body, so fluids are given as ordered and the doctor told.

Key Clue: falling urine output after severe burns

Priority Principle: Burn shock

Why Not Others: (a) Holding fluids worsens the loss; (c) Walking is unsafe in burn shock; (d) Waiting an hour risks the kidneys.

PGI Exam Trap: Her fluids are held back to reduce the swelling.

5-Second Recall: Give fluids as ordered and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Burns and less urine mean give fluids.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a hot water bottle safely to a woman with pain. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Check the skin, wrap the bottle, then put it on the area
option_2: Put the bottle on the skin FIRST and then wrap it
option_3: Wrap the bottle, put it on the skin, then check the rule
option_4: Put the bottle on bare skin to feel the heat
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check the skin, wrap the bottle, then put it on the area

Clinical Rationale: The nurse checks the skin, wraps the hot water bottle in a cloth, and then puts it on the area, so the skin is NOT burnt.

Key Clue: the steps for giving a hot water bottle

Priority Principle: Hot water bottle order

Why Not Others: (b) A bare bottle on the skin may burn it; (c) Checking the rule and skin comes first; (d) A bottle on bare skin can burn the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: The bottle is put on bare skin to feel the heat.

5-Second Recall: Check the skin, wrap the bottle, then put it on the area.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check, wrap, then apply.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a newborn its FIRST breast feed. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Wrap the baby warm and give it to the family
option_2: Help it to suckle FIRST and then dry the baby
option_3: Place it on the mother, help it to suckle, then dry it
option_4: Dry the baby, place it on the mother, then help it to suckle
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Dry the baby, place it on the mother, then help it to suckle

Clinical Rationale: The newborn is dried, placed on the mother, and then helped to suckle, so that it stays warm and takes the FIRST milk.

Key Clue: the steps for the FIRST breast feed

Priority Principle: First feed order

Why Not Others: (a) The first feed is given by the mother, not the family; (b) The baby is dried before it is put to the breast; (c) Drying the baby comes first of all.

PGI Exam Trap: The baby is given to the family before the FIRST feed.

5-Second Recall: Dry the baby, place it on the mother, then help it to suckle.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry, place, then feed.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the postnatal ward is asked which statement about a normal blood loss after birth is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is bright red with large clots for a full month
option_2: It is a heavy flow that never lessens day by day
option_3: It is a moderate flow that slowly becomes less over some days
option_4: It stops the moment the baby is born
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It is a moderate flow that slowly becomes less over some days

Clinical Rationale: Normal blood loss after birth is a moderate flow that slowly becomes less over some days, as the womb heals inside.

Key Clue: the normal blood loss after birth

Priority Principle: Postpartum blood loss

Why Not Others: (a) Large bright red clots for a month are not normal; (b) A heavy flow that never lessens is not normal; (d) Some loss continues for a few days.

PGI Exam Trap: The loss stops the moment the baby is born.

5-Second Recall: It is a moderate flow that slowly becomes less over days.

PNC Exam Pearl: Moderate, then slowly less.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to record the vital signs of a man who has just come in. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Take the pulse while he is still walking in
option_2: Take the blood pressure FIRST while he walks in
option_3: Let him rest, then take the pulse, then the blood pressure
option_4: Take the readings while he is talking loudly
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Let him rest, then take the pulse, then the blood pressure

Clinical Rationale: The nurse lets the man rest and then takes the pulse and the blood pressure, so the readings are true and NOT raised by movement.

Key Clue: the steps for recording vital signs

Priority Principle: Vital signs order

Why Not Others: (a) A pulse while walking is not a true rest value; (b) A reading while he walks in is raised; (d) Talking raises the readings.

PGI Exam Trap: The readings are taken while he walks in and talks.

5-Second Recall: Let him rest, then take the pulse, then the blood pressure.

PNC Exam Pearl: Rest first, then read.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse manager on the ward must set the order of steps to manage a unit that is short of nurses tonight. In which order should the manager take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Leave the duty list and hope the night runs well
option_2: Inform the seniors FIRST and then check the ward needs
option_3: Set the duty list, check the needs, then inform the seniors
option_4: Check the ward needs, set the duty list, then inform the seniors
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the ward needs, set the duty list, then inform the seniors

Clinical Rationale: The manager checks the needs of the ward, sets the duty list to cover them, and then informs the seniors, so safe care is planned.

Key Clue: setting the duty list when the ward is short of nurses

Priority Principle: Duty list planning

Why Not Others: (a) Leaving the duty list risks unsafe care; (b) Needs are checked before the seniors are told; (c) Checking the needs comes first of all.

PGI Exam Trap: The duty list is left and the night is left to chance.

5-Second Recall: Check the ward needs, set the duty list, then inform the seniors.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check needs, set list, then tell.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a head injury notes that he is becoming drowsy and his pulse is slowing. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Check his airway and call for help
option_2: Give him a drink and let him rest
option_3: Ask him to walk to test his balance
option_4: Note it and wait for the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check his airway and call for help

Clinical Rationale: Drowsiness with a slowing pulse after a head injury points to rising pressure in the brain, so his airway is checked and help called at once.

Key Clue: drowsiness with a slowing pulse after a head injury

Priority Principle: Raised brain pressure

Why Not Others: (b) A drink while drowsy risks choking; (c) Walking is unsafe with this sign; (d) Waiting for the round risks his life.

PGI Exam Trap: The sign is noted and the ward round is awaited.

5-Second Recall: Check his airway and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Drowsy and slow pulse mean call for help.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse visits a home where a man with a long term illness has been on the same medicine for many months without a review. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell him to stop all medicine at once
option_2: Review his medicine with the doctor and check his progress
option_3: Ask him to double every dose at home
option_4: Leave the medicine and take no action
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Review his medicine with the doctor and check his progress

Clinical Rationale: A long term medicine needs a proper review, so the nurse checks it with the doctor and looks at the man's progress.

Key Clue: a man on the same medicine for months without review

Priority Principle: Medicine review

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping all medicine at once may harm him; (c) Doubling doses at home is dangerous; (d) Taking no action leaves him unreviewed.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is told to stop all his medicine at once.

5-Second Recall: Review his medicine with the doctor and check his progress.

PNC Exam Pearl: Old medicine needs a fresh review.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is very anxious before an operation notes that he cannot sit still and asks many questions. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Sit with him and answer his questions calmly
option_2: Tell him to stop asking so many questions
option_3: Leave him alone till the operation time
option_4: Give him a strong drink to calm him
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Sit with him and answer his questions calmly

Clinical Rationale: Sitting with the anxious man and answering his questions calmly helps to ease his fear before the operation.

Key Clue: an anxious man asking many questions

Priority Principle: Preoperative anxiety

Why Not Others: (b) Telling him to stop adds to his fear; (c) Leaving him alone lets the fear grow; (d) A strong drink is unsafe before surgery.

PGI Exam Trap: He is left alone till the operation time.

5-Second Recall: Sit with him and answer his questions calmly.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sit, listen, answer calmly.

question: A nurse on the ward is pricked by a needle used on a man with a blood borne virus. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Cover it and finish the round FIRST
option_2: Wash the wound and report the injury at once
option_3: Squeeze the wound hard to make it bleed
option_4: Wait and see if any illness appears
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Wash the wound and report the injury at once

Clinical Rationale: After a needle prick the wound is washed and the injury reported at once, so that any treatment is started early.

Key Clue: a needle prick from a man with a blood borne virus

Priority Principle: Needle stick injury

Why Not Others: (a) Finishing the round delays the report; (c) Squeezing the wound may cause more harm; (d) Waiting lets the chance of care pass.

PGI Exam Trap: The wound is covered and the round is finished FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Wash the wound and report the injury at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Wash it, report it, now.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is on a course of an antibiotic for many days develops a sore mouth with white patches. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop all fluids and all food
option_2: Give a stronger antibiotic at once
option_3: Report it and give mouth care as ordered
option_4: Ignore it as it will settle on its own
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report it and give mouth care as ordered

Clinical Rationale: A sore mouth with white patches on long antibiotics points to a fungal infection, so it is reported and mouth care is given as ordered.

Key Clue: a sore mouth with white patches on antibiotics

Priority Principle: Oral thrush

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping fluids and food weakens him; (b) A stronger antibiotic does not treat a fungus; (d) Ignoring it lets the infection spread.

PGI Exam Trap: A stronger antibiotic is given at once for the white patches.

5-Second Recall: Report it and give mouth care as ordered.

PNC Exam Pearl: White patches on antibiotics mean thrush.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who is given a drug by drip notes that the site of the drip is red and warm and she has a fever. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and check the drip next hour
option_2: Speed up the drip to clear the site
option_3: Warm the site with a hot pack
option_4: Stop the drip and tell the doctor at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Stop the drip and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A red warm drip site with a fever points to an infection in the vein, so the drip is stopped and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: a red warm drip site with a fever

Priority Principle: Infusion site infection

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting an hour lets the infection spread; (b) Speeding up the drip spreads the infection; (c) A hot pack makes the site worse.

PGI Exam Trap: The drip is speeded up to clear the site.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drip and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Red warm site with fever means stop the drip.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).
